run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T16:44:18Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert under investigation (labels/annotations as supplied, untrusted: RequestErrorRate, warning, service_name=frontend-proxy, namespace=otel-demo, current 0.0333, since 2026-11-16T16:44:18Z) is consistent with sustained nonzero error spans on frontend-proxy's own ingress operation. The spanmetrics counter for service_name=frontend-proxy, span_name="ingress", status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR stood at 557 at the first available sample (16:17:00) and 588 at 16:49:00, i.e. 31 further error spans in 31 minutes, while total ingress spans rose from 8,342 to 29,084 (20,742 spans); the counter increments in most minutes rather than in one burst. The frontend-proxy pod's own access logs explain those errors: every 5xx observed in the sampled windows is HTTP 503 with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, with upstream fields naming frontend and the frontend Service ClusterIP 100.70.94.93:8080, whose sole endpoint is pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh (Deployment frontend). That frontend pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, has no ERROR-status spans of its own, keeps a steady GET/POST p99 of 739-874 ms, holds ~128.7 MB against a 200Mi limit, and all five nodes are Ready without pressure conditions. The evidence therefore localizes the failures to upstream connections to the frontend Deployment that are terminated before a response starts; it does not establish why the frontend side closes them, because the Envoy configuration is baked into the image (no frontend-proxy ConfigMap exists), the frontend container produced no application log lines, and no trace data exists in Jaeger after about 16:17:13. A pre-existing accumulation of 557 error spans happened between the collector start (~16:04) and the first scrape (16:17); its timing inside that interval is unknown. The alert's reported value 0.0333 could not be reproduced from the span metrics, and the RequestErrorRate rule itself could not be located in this Prometheus.

claims.text: The only ERROR-status span series for frontend-proxy in the window is span_name="ingress" with span_kind SPAN_KIND_SERVER (exported_job opentelemetry-demo/frontend-proxy, a single series); its cumulative value was 557 at the first sample 16:17:00 and 588 at 16:49:00, i.e. +31 error spans in 31 minutes.

Total frontend-proxy ingress spans rose from 8,342 (16:18:00) to 29,084 (16:49:00), 20,742 spans in 31 minutes (~669/min), so the 31 error spans added in that interval correspond to an ingress error ratio of about 0.0015 (0.15%).

The frontend-proxy ingress error counter increased in most minutes between 16:17 and 16:49 with deltas of 1-4 per minute (557 to 559 to 560 to 561 to 563, and so on), showing a sustained trickle rather than one discrete burst.

The frontend-proxy pod access logs show the corresponding failures as HTTP 503 with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}: 21 such lines from 16:17:32 to 16:31:56 (read stopped at the 4 MiB limit) and 10 such lines from 16:35:46 to 16:48:00, all with upstream fields "frontend" and "100.70.94.93:8080", client python-requests from 100.96.2.17, on routes /, /api/cart, /api/products/*, /api/recommendations and /api/data.

Outside those 503s the sampled frontend-proxy access-log stream shows successful traffic: 200 responses and 308 redirects for /api/data/ trailing-slash requests (GET /, /api/products/*, /api/cart, /api/checkout, /api/data) between 16:48:01 and 16:48:11.

Kubernetes Service frontend has ClusterIP 100.70.94.93 on port 8080 with exactly one endpoint, 100.96.2.139:8080, which is pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh, owned by ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5, owned by Deployment frontend; this is the 100.70.94.93:8080 upstream address named in the failing proxy log lines.
Pods frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p6mgt are both Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no last terminated container state, started at 16:04:22-16:04:24.

The frontend service's own spans carry no ERROR status in the window (STATUS_CODE_ERROR is 0 for its GET, POST and /api/* and grpc client operations), while its GET|POST span counter rose from 8,306 (16:18) to 29,038 (16:49), i.e. 20,732 spans, within about 10 of the proxy's 20,742 ingress spans.
Frontend GET/POST span p99 stayed between 739 ms and 874 ms at every 5-minute point from 16:25 to 16:50, so no latency degradation accompanied the 503s.

Working-set memory stayed well below container limits: frontend peaked at 128,720,896 bytes (~128.7 MB against a 200Mi limit) and frontend-proxy at 20,627,456 bytes (~20.6 MB against a 50Mi limit) during the window.
The frontend container was CPU-throttled in every sampled minute from 16:18 to 16:48, with a throttled-periods ratio between 0.21 and 0.42; frontend-proxy was throttled at about 0.05 at 16:49.
All five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False, including i-030aedeb6471c8a81, which hosts both the frontend and frontend-proxy pods.

All 21 otel-demo deployments report 1/1 available and ready; ReplicaSets were created at 16:04:21-16:04:23 and the only rollout visible in the window is flagd (new ReplicaSet flagd-7f6c6df658 created 16:06:15, old flagd-c47676d99 scaled to 0), i.e. the stack was redeployed about 40 minutes before the alert.
Neither the frontend nor the frontend-proxy container defines a readiness, liveness or startup probe (all three probe fields are null in both Deployment specs).

ERROR-status span series elsewhere are small and on different operations: ad 2.04, fraud-detection 2.04 and recommendation 4.06 on flagd EventStream operations (ad: flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, fraud-detection: flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, recommendation: /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream), while accounting, frontend and payment read 0.
The fraud-detection container was OOMKilled (exit code 137, finishedAt 16:09:47) with restartCount 1 and is now Ready - a change in a different service about 35 minutes before the alert.

Leading explanation: the frontend-side HTTP server is closing connections that frontend-proxy's Envoy upstream pool reuses (an idle keep-alive or timeout mismatch), so a small fraction of dispatched requests hit a socket the upstream already terminated and Envoy records 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}. It fits a steady ~1-1.5 failures/min out of ~669 requests/min against a frontend that is up, un-restarted, error-free in its own spans and steady in latency, but the Envoy cluster settings and the frontend's Node.js server settings could not be read to confirm it.

Alternative candidate: the frontend container's persistent CPU throttling (21%-42% of CFS periods at its 100m limit) occasionally starves the Node.js process enough to drop in-flight connections. This is weak: throttling is continuous across the whole window while only a small subset of requests fails, and no minute-level correlation between throttling and error increments was established.

Additional candidate: the 557 error spans already present at the first sample (16:17:00) came from a startup transient in which frontend-proxy served traffic before the frontend could accept it (neither deployment has readiness probes and the pods plus load generator started at 16:04:2x). This could explain a longer-window error ratio of a few percent, but it does not explain the continued ~1/min 503s after 16:17.

The frontend's own signals show no application failure: restartCount 0 with no last termination state, 0 ERROR spans across its operations, p99 steady at 739-874 ms and memory at ~64% of its limit, so the resets are not explained by a frontend crash, OOM or latency collapse.

The frontend's server-span count for the same interval (20,732 GET|POST spans) is within about 10 of the proxy's total ingress span count (20,742), so the ~31 failed requests leave no visible deficit at the frontend; this comparison cannot localize the reset to the frontend process versus the path between Envoy and the pod.
Frontend pod crash/restart or OOM as the cause of the 503s is rejected: the frontend container has restartCount 0 and no last terminated state in the window.
Node-level resource exhaustion as the cause is rejected: all five nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False.

The fraud-detection OOMKill at 16:09:47 (exit 137) is rejected as this alert's cause: it is a different service affected 35 minutes before the alert, the alert is scoped to frontend-proxy, and fraud-detection's own error spans are on a flagd EventStream operation rather than HTTP ingress.

The flagd EventStream ERROR spans in ad (2.04), recommendation (4.06) and fraud-detection (2.04) are rejected as the alert's source: they belong to different services and different operations (flagd streaming), not to frontend-proxy ingress spans.

Reconcile how the alert is computed with the observed data: the frontend-proxy ingress error counter moved from 557 to 588 (+31) while total ingress spans moved from 8,342 to 29,084, and the 5-minute ingress error ratio sampled between 16:19 and 16:49 was 0.0004-0.0030, so the alert's reported 0.0333 should be traced in the Alertmanager rule source.

Compare the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream cluster settings for the frontend cluster (idle timeout, max requests per connection, retries) with the frontend's HTTP keep-alive settings and align them so Envoy stops reusing connections the frontend has already closed; enabling retries on reset-before-response would also cut user-visible 503s.

Add readiness probes to the frontend and frontend-proxy deployments (neither currently has any probe) and capture the frontend container's stdout/stderr, so startup-time 5xx and any application-level cause of connection termination become observable.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule could not be located in this Prometheus: the rule lookup for RequestErrorRate returned status no_data (7b9257c1-8f22-435a-a88c-6c31a34bf426-t0:fd8b09d6-9956-4656-aaab-891906be6ec3) and the alerting-rule listing returned status no_data with no groups (1eab89df-f62b-4794-a569-80a32782ee9b-t1:cdc0b096-672a-401d-bf06-99a33bfc60c7), so the alert expression, window, threshold and the reported current value 0.0333 remain unverified rather than zero or false.

The frontend-proxy Envoy configuration is unavailable: no frontend-proxy ConfigMap exists in otel-demo (the ConfigMaps found are flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products), the configuration is baked into the ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy image, so upstream idle timeouts, connection-reuse limits and retry policy could not be checked.

The frontend container produced no application log lines in the queried windows: the frontend log fetch for 16:04-16:20 returned status no_data (550bed78-fc6b-489c-b0b2-5c725a9fc0f3-t1:15f1ae54-e23e-42b3-b4d3-1f909eb9c445), the fetch for 16:30-16:51 with an error filter returned status no_data (8d3440d6-28f2-4de1-9afb-b3319db1f480-t1:60bb2347-ba48-4314-b85b-6a41012007a8), and the unfiltered fetch for 16:35-16:51 also returned status no_data (a5cb4417-7c25-4d55-937c-0e7719c0ce70-t1:56a1594f-d97f-4caa-a3ed-58c548a782c5); thus no frontend-side log evidence exists for why its HTTP server terminates connections.

Jaeger held no trace data at or after the alert time: the trace search for frontend-proxy in 16:43-16:45 returned status no_data (550bed78-fc6b-489c-b0b2-5c725a9fc0f3-t0:deee350a-4100-46d2-8ef9-c839e9eedb95) and the stored span sample covers only 16:17:09-16:17:13 (8cefddc0-7600-4eaf-94d7-57dcfa1f7a14-t0:5e24ec5e-6c7d-4599-8df7-25667f8fd070, truncated), so the failing requests at 16:44 could not be inspected at trace level.

Span tag searches for the failing status codes were inconclusive: searches tagged http.status_code="500" (841117ec-ccbc-40cc-a601-324444acbcde-t1:450c06b6-653d-4f76-9b2e-f4c1302222d5), "503" and "429" (aaaf19b3-bc51-403f-9944-5195985c01e5-t0:8d37d421-6b3c-4efa-ba41-6d01ece96870 and aaaf19b3-bc51-403f-9944-5195985c01e5-t1:bb3b16e5-cb47-43fd-97c3-d3939eeea300) returned no_data; only the access logs name the 503 code, so a trace-level confirmation of the status breakdown is missing.

Kubernetes events for otel-demo returned status no_data (550bed78-fc6b-489c-b0b2-5c725a9fc0f3-t2:f4aaefc0-8072-4d96-b94a-10cef9ef3e2f), so there is no event-level record of restarts, probe failures or scheduling around the window.

The 557 ingress error spans already accumulated at the first spanmetric sample (16:17:00) occurred between the collector start (~16:04:30) and 16:17:00; no per-minute samples exist before 16:17, so that initial accumulation's distribution is unknown.
Change history is not an available integration, so no record of any configuration change at the ~16:04 redeployment could be checked.

No per-route or per-status Envoy metrics are exposed through this Prometheus (only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket carry service_name=frontend-proxy), so per-path error rates and 4xx/5xx breakdowns beyond the access-log sample are unknown.
next_steps: Pull the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Alertmanager rule source and confirm which metric and labels it divides and what threshold it uses, to reconcile the reported 0.0333 with the observed ~0.0015 ingress error ratio.

Diff the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream cluster configuration for the frontend cluster against the frontend's HTTP keep-alive and timeout settings, and consider lowering Envoy's upstream idle timeout or enabling retries on reset-before-response.
Enable and collect frontend application logs and add readiness probes to the frontend and frontend-proxy deployments so resets on the frontend side become observable.
If the alert should remain meaningful, consider an evaluation delay or an absolute error-count condition so a steady ~1/min reset trickle does not page on a ratio that rounds to a few percent.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
